A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LD3M research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet classification experiments, component ablations, diffusion-step analyses, and distilled-image examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds CIFAR-10 evaluation, initialization experiments, and computational-resource measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same pretrained LDM, learnable latent and conditioning codes, residual interpolation, encoder-based initialization, and checkpointing procedure. Gaussian initialization in v3 Table 5 is an experimental control, not a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds lower-resolution CIFAR-10 classification evaluation in Table 4 alongside the retained ImageNet subsets at 128×128 and 256×256. This extends data and resolution coverage within the existing classification task. Additional ImageNet-D/E appendix grids illustrate already evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Matched ImageNet comparisons and the component ablation retain their comparator membership. The new CIFAR-10 evaluation uses existing pixel-space and GLaD comparator families, including trained and random generators. Newly discussed work by Zhong et al. is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Existing ImageNet architectures, budgets, evaluation procedures, and diffusion-step defaults are retained. v3 adds a controlled Gaussian-versus-real-image initialization comparison at IPC=1 and 5,000 iterations, CIFAR-10 evaluation with DC/DM across four architectures, and peak GPU allocation as an additional resource metric.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 adds a focused initialization-sensitivity study across MTT, DC, and DM. The existing component ablation moves from v1 Table 4 to v3 Table 6 unchanged; diffusion-step sensitivity, collapse examples, and generator-pretraining comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five evaluation repetitions and report mean validation accuracy plus or minus one standard deviation. Figure 4 retains its uncertainty display, and the new tables follow the existing reporting practice. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Although all values in the retained result tables match, v3 substantially expands reported outcomes. New CIFAR-10 LD3M/GLaD trained-generator averages are 28.6/26.3 for DC and 23.4/23.8 for DM. It adds initialization findings, LD3M/GLaD total times of 574/693 minutes, A100 memory usage of 29.4/31.2 GB, and four appendix image grids. These are added results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the GAN-inversion optimization expression, and checkpointing derivations retain their mathematical content. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical corrections appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: diffusion-based latent distillation, improved gradient propagation and cross-architecture performance, straightforward initialization, and an adjustable speed-quality trade-off. The headline gains remain 4.8 and 4.2 percentage points; stronger wording does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the initialization results as showing stronger dependence on real images for DC/DM than MTT and adds discussion of memory flexibility. It removes v1's speculation that alternative interpolation strategies would not substantially improve quality with the same pretrained LDM. The large-timestep vanishing-gradient limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds A100-40GB hardware and timing/peak-memory documentation. Existing appendix details—including guidance scale, learning rates, augmentation, batch sizes, and MTT expert trajectories—are retained. No new code or data access information is provided.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhong et al.'s Hierarchical Features Matter and contrasts its hierarchical latent-space search with LD3M's single latent space. It also adds DiffusedHeads and removes the StyleGAN3/Alias-free GAN reference. Positioning relative to GLaD, Duan et al., and minimax diffusion remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 tightens the abstract and makes sentence-level edits across the introduction, background, and method explanations while retaining the scientific narrative and main section sequence. It adds a short Societal Impact section and replaces the acknowledgment placeholder with funding information.

P2.justification: The main paper and references switch from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. v3 adds two result tables and four appendix image grids, numbers the existing hyperparameter table, and moves the class-listing table to the final page. Existing figures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added CIFAR-10 evaluation, initialization-sensitivity evidence, and resource measurements improve empirical breadth and practical guidance while preserving the original method and results. Reporting precision is weakened by an unexplained DC/ImageNette discrepancy: v3 Table 1 gives 32.9±1.2, whereas Table 5 gives 32.9±2.1. Overall, the added evidence supports a limited net improvement.
